supporting_observations.claim: The supplied records do not identify backupadmin or show a domain-account creation event. The record closest to the alert time shows Kerberos traffic from WS-KNGUYEN-01 to the domain controller, but does not identify the account or action involved.

The supplied evidence includes LDAP connections from WS-KNGUYEN-01 to the domain controller, including one after the alert time, but the connection records do not reveal the LDAP operations or prove account creation.

At 14:18 UTC, the domain controller recorded a network logon by the WS-KNGUYEN-01 machine account, followed shortly by logoff; these records do not establish that backupadmin was created or identify a human actor.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records show network connections and authentication events, but do not include an account-creation audit event or the contents of the LDAP operations. Relevant examples are the LDAP connection records T117-00013 and T117-00183.
The supplied records do not identify who initiated the alerted account creation or what privileges or group memberships, if any, were assigned.
claims_not_established: Whether backupadmin was actually created during the review window.
Which person or process created backupadmin, and from which host.

additional_evidence_needed: Domain-controller security audit logs for account creation and modification events (including event 4720 and relevant group-membership events) during the review window.
Directory Service change auditing, including event 5136 if available, to identify the object changes and actor.
Correlated logon and process-creation evidence for the account creator, including relevant endpoint PowerShell or command-line logs.
Current and historical group memberships, privileges, and sign-in activity for backupadmin.
